source.publication: 2025 Maryland Resident Booklet (State and Local Tax Forms and Instructions), Form 502
source.section: Form 502 Lines 1, 13 (Form 502SU code u), 14-21; Instruction 13 Line 13 code letter u (PDF page 17); Schedule II (PDF page 22)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = military retired pay (you) 25,000.00 + wages (spouse) 40,000.00 + military retired pay (spouse) 15,000.00 = 80,000.00. Federal taxable income = 80,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 48,500.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form 502 Line 1 federal AGI 80,000.00; Lines 2-6 additions 0.00 (no non-Maryland municipal interest); Line 7 total 80,000.00. Form 502SU: code u (you, age 60, 55 or older): smaller of military retirement 25,000.00 and 20,000.00 = 20,000.00; code u (spouse, age 50, under 55): smaller of military retirement 15,000.00 and 12,500.00 = 12,500.00. Line 13 = 32,500.00. Line 14 two-income subtraction: 1,200.00 on the form (both spouses have Maryland income); the projection does not apply it, see the approximation note at the end. Line 15 total subtractions = Line 13 32,500.00 = 32,500.00. Line 16 Maryland AGI = 80,000.00 - 32,500.00 = 47,500.00. Line 17 standard deduction (Instruction 16, flat by filing status) = 6,700.00. Line 18 net income = 47,500.00 - 6,700.00 = 40,800.00. Line 19 exemptions: Chart 10A at federal AGI 80,000.00 (not over 150,000) gives 3,200.00 each x 2 (Box A) = 6,400.00. Line 20 taxable net income = 40,800.00 - 6,400.00 = 34,400.00. Line 21 tax, Schedule II as numbers: 2.00% x 1,000.00 = 20.00 + 3.00% x 1,000.00 = 30.00 + 4.00% x 1,000.00 = 40.00 + 4.75% x 31,400.00 = 1,491.50; total 1,581.50. (The tax table row 34,400-34,450, PDF page 36, gives 1,583; expected keeps the formula figure.) Lines 22-26 credits: none modelled or claimed, 0.00; Maryland state tax 1,581.50. Local tax (Lines 28-33) out of scope; 2% capital gain tax (Line 21b) not charged (no gains, AGI under 350,000). Line 14 (Worksheet 13D, PDF page 18): the form would subtract the smaller of 1,200 and the lower spouse's income after subtractions = 1,200.00, lowering tax by 1,200 x 4.75% = 57.00; the projection does not apply it (approximation), so expected shows 0.00 here. Whose age counts: each spouse's own age sets his or her own limit (20,000 at 60, 12,500 at 50); both are over their limits.
accepted_approximations: The two-income married couple subtraction is not applied.
